situation: A married woman reissuing her passport wanted to change her surname from her maiden name to her married name, along with her address. An ad agency said a newspaper notice and a notarised affidavit were needed, which the family found confusing.

remedies_reported.name: Email the local passport officer with the documents and ask which documents are needed
Carry the marriage certificate or Annexure J (bringing both is safest), plus a printout of the officer's reply
Publish a newspaper notice of the name change with a notarised affidavit

conflict_note: The official document advisory says a surname change after marriage needs only a marriage certificate or Annexure J. At the counter, staff still asked why there was no newspaper notice, so practice at the counter can differ from the published rule.
your_summary: Different people gave the family different answers about changing a wife's surname after marriage. The passport officer confirmed by email that a marriage certificate or Annexure J was enough. At the appointment, staff questioned the missing newspaper notice and the officer in charge took about two hours, but the change was approved.
